title: Clear a bent staple from a cordless stapler
instruction: Clear the jam and leave the stapler ready to reload.
justification: A blocked fastener driver requires physical access and obstruction extraction; the installed battery and residual drive compression create a documented accidental actuation/ejection hazard. Goal does not specify isolation.
fault: Ryobi P361 narrow-crown staple bent into its driver path, holding driver down; no invented manual-T50 cocked spring.
objects: Removable battery and actual latch geometry to implement after access gate
skill: Isolate energy, open actual sliding magazine, push blocked driver back through narrow service opening, remove bent staple, leave channel clear and magazine usable. Safe alternatives accepted; no named tool required.
scoring: Draft only: actual bent staple outside tool, driver clearance restored, magazine empty and serviceable, battery disconnected, robot released, with permanent record of unsafe access while connected. No paper/wood penetration or test firing needed for ready-to-reload goal.
nearest: PR1276 accepted: load correctly oriented staple strip with spring follower; no driver obstruction extraction
PR1467 pending: unloaded nailer carry with orientation/trigger avoidance; no service mechanism
BEHAVIOR stapler only desk tidying in current object-synset task list
risks: Reviewer may see generic power-tool service as insufficient distinction; estimate acceptance0.23 before physical gate
Driver preload/retention and precise internal clearances require disclosed estimates and physical validation

source_observations: Manual p10 and Fig11 p13 explicitly use flat screwdriver to push driver back then remove bent staple. p3 warns possible compression and forceful discharge. Fig5 shows sliding bottom-load magazine. 18GA narrow crown 3/8–1.5inch staples,105 capacity from Ryobi.
status: bounded mechanism gate blocked; access passed, passive jam not validated
